jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create one polished revised 16:9 full game-scene illustration.
Image 1: scene to edit. Image 2: exact ornamental source; use ONLY its central three-eyed diamond medallion and surrounding interwoven arcs/four-point star details, not the whole card frame or stats.
The previous table embroidery is WRONG because it is merely generic looping curves. Replace it with a LARGE faithful three-eye diamond medallion from image 2, rendered as raised gold-thread embroidery directly on emerald green velvet.
The tabletop is a horizontal plane receding away from the camera. The embroidered emblem MUST be projected onto this plane: a foreshortened wide rhombus/diamond with four STRAIGHT crisp double-gold edges and four obvious vertices, NOT an upright diamond facing the viewer and NOT a generic oval. Its back tip is near the center just in front of the slot's feet; its side tips reach far to left and right beyond the row of played cards; its front tip is close to the foreground table edge. Its geometry is continuous beneath occluding objects. Surround it with the card's interlacing loops, subordinate to the STRAIGHT diamond boundary.
Inside the diamond reproduce EXACTLY THREE almond-shaped eyes with dark pupils: one centered at the rear/top, two side-by-side toward the foreground/bottom, with eyelash-like short rays as in image 2. All eyes follow the same perspective plane as the diamond. Embroidered gold eye contours and iris fill, dark green/black pupils. Do not add a fourth eye. This is the card back's recognizable central emblem, enlarged across the playable table.
COMPOSITION: Give the fore-table enough depth to show the embroidery meaningfully. Slightly adjust card row spacing/position backward if necessary to reveal the lower pair of large eyes in the foreground; retain all three existing cards, full machine, deck left, detail slip below it, mushroom right, lever with horizontal side pivot. The large diamond's left and right vertices, long lower diagonal edges and foreground vertex must be clearly visible OUTSIDE the objects, so viewers still recognize a diamond lying in perspective even with the table occupied. The embroidered three eyes belong underneath the objects, never printed on top of cards or slot. Aim for portions of the eyes visible in the open foreground; the empty-table version must reveal the complete three-eyed emblem.
Raised gilt thread has fine stitches, small relief shadows, bright gold edging on deep green velvet. A deliberate legible large emblem rather than random busy flourishes. Retain the illustrated ink/engraved style, controlled hatching, same starry open sky, same deep petrol/brass cabinet, bulbs above/below, suit and attack markings on reels, cards/art style and HUD/LEGENDA. No room, no candles or extra props, no NEON MONTE/ATTACCA/GIRA or empty plaques. Preserve the successful overall scene and only improve the TABLE MOTIF, table perspective/foreground space and minimal card spacing necessary to display it.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this exact full game composition with one targeted correction ONLY to the embroidered table medallion.
The giant three-eye gold embroidered diamond on the green velvet is good, but its foreground diamond point is cut off at the bottom of the image. Correct its projection/size: compress the entire embroidered medallion slightly along the table's receding-depth direction, so the FRONTMOST DIAMOND VERTEX is fully visible at approximately 93 percent of image height, leaving a clear 6-7 percent image-height strip of GREEN VELVET between the complete gold design and the bottom image edge. Its left and right vertices remain widely spaced outside the card row, its back point stays near the slot feet. It is one closed straight-edged double-line DIAMOND lying on the horizontal table plane, with four corners, exactly THREE embroidered almond eyes arranged one rear/top and two front/bottom, interlacing arcs and four-point stars faithfully following the same perspective. The two lower eyes can sit slightly higher but remain partially visible below the cards. Do not crop any lower diagonal edge or the front vertex. Keep the embroidery gold raised thread and all other pixels/objects/composition as close as possible: machine, sky, lamp bulbs, lever, red mushroom, all three cards at same scale and positions, deck, detail sheet and HUD. Do not change the camera or zoom the full image. Do not add plaques or labels or any objects. Stylized ink and engraving style unchanged.

Use case: precise-object-edit / background-extraction. Derive the clean EMPTY TABLE AND SKY background from this exact illustrated game scene.
Remove ALL foreground objects and UI: the whole slot machine including feet/lever/lights, the deck, all three played cards, detail sheet, red mushroom button, upper-left stats parchment and upper-right LEGENDA button. Remove their cast/contact shadows. Inpaint their footprints with the continuous green velvet table surface and open starry sky behind.
CRITICAL: Preserve the camera framing and tabletop/sky boundary, the green velvet table perspective and every already-visible part of the GOLD THREE-EYE DIAMOND MEDALLION exactly in place and same size. Do not zoom or enlarge or recenter the table emblem. Complete only the currently occluded portions under the cards/objects. The resulting empty table must reveal ONE closed gold double-line rhombus lying in perspective, with all FOUR vertices within image frame and precisely THREE embroidered almond eyes INSIDE it: one rear eye centered near the back tip, TWO forward eyes arranged side by side. The three eyes must be recognizable as the SAME motif already visible around the cards in the source. Complete continuous straight diamond edges and the interlaced ornamental loops, little eyelash rays and four-point stars underneath removed objects. No extra eyes or a duplicate medallion. Gold is raised embroidered thread with small relief highlights on deep green velvet; no blank rectangular footprints.
No new objects, no text, no signs, no buildings or interiors. ONLY the EMPTY emerald velvet gaming TABLE bearing its completed gold three-eye diamond embroidery, with the same open star-filled sky as backdrop. Retain illustrated ink linework and engraving/hatching; same wide 16:9 frame.
